decision_rule: p-hacking only if the full-registry KS test does not reject uniformity at 0.05 and the one-sided exact-binomial test finds excess cited p<0.05 at 0.05
ks_caveat: P-values are pooled across seeds; pairwise tests within a dataset share columns, so the classical KS reference p-value is diagnostic and may be miscalibrated. The two-sample KS comparison also reuses the reported subset from the full registry.
result_paragraph: Across 100 null datasets, the full registry contained 19000 tests (KS D=0.0056, p=0.5932); reported claims cited 967 p-values, of which 1.000 were below 0.05 (one-sided exact-binomial p=0). Pre-registered classification: p-hacking.
